All 90 participants with gaze data are processed (None 35, Partial 35, Full 20; 89 included in the analyses, 15265 is excluded). The left eye was recorded in 85 of them, the right eye in 5. Participants 11872 and 5272 contribute the trials of their truncated files (163 and 13 trials). EyeLink pupil size is a diameter in arbitrary units; the participant median ranges from 4,073 to 8,926 units.
The pupil stream consists of 20 ms bins: the mean of the valid 1000 Hz samples in the bin and the share of valid samples (valid = pupil size above 0 and gaze on record;
). Each trial is one recording block, which starts about 200 ms before the colour cue and ends at the end of the outcome phase.
The steps are applied to each recording block (trial) of each participant:
bins with any invalid 1000 Hz sample (blink or tracking loss)
bins within 100 ms before and 160 ms after a missing bin are removed; the pupil signal is distorted while the lid closes and opens
speed = larger of the absolute changes to the previous and the next bin, per 20 ms; bins above the participant median + 10 × MAD are removed (Kret & Sjak-Shie, 2019)
gaps up to 500 ms within a trial are interpolated linearly; longer gaps and gaps at the start or end of a trial stay missing
4 Hz low-pass filter (Butterworth, third order, zero phase) on stretches of at least 500 ms without missing bins

A trial is usable for pupil analyses when at most 25 % of the bins from the cue onset to the end of the ISI are missing after interpolation and the cue baseline is present. Of 16,008 trials, 13,602 are usable (85 %). The cue baseline lies in the first 200 ms of the recording and is missing in 10.8 % of the trials; 6.9 % of the trials have more than 25 % missing bins. Per participant the median share of usable trials is 89 % (28–100 %); below 50 % are 16381 (28 %), 15289 (43 %), 15265 (48 %, excluded) and 13855 (49 %). No participant or trial is removed by the script.
